FINANCE
Procurement Policy
Approval thresholds, competitive quotations, vendor onboarding, evaluation and procure-to-pay controls
Document ID
NX-FIN-002
Version
3.0
Document
owner
Head of Procurement (CFO Office)
Effective date
1 January 2026
Applies to
All departments purchasing goods or
services
Classification
Internal - Confidential
Abstract. This policy establishes how Nexora buys goods and services. It sets approval authority and quotation
requirements by purchase value, defines the vendor onboarding and evaluation process, and describes the procure-to-pay
workflow including three-way matching and payment terms. The objectives are value for money, transparency, segregation
of duties and compliance with tax and legal requirements in Pakistan.
Keywords: procurement, purchase order, quotations, RFP, vendor onboarding, approval matrix, three-way match
1. Objectives and Roles
• Requester: raises the purchase requisition with business justification and budget code.
• Department head: confirms the need and budget availability.
• Procurement team: runs quotations and tenders, negotiates and issues purchase orders (POs).
• Finance: checks budget, matches invoices and releases payment.
• Legal and InfoSec: review contracts and software or cloud purchases that process company or customer
data.
Rule: No commitment may be made to a vendor, verbally or in writing, before a PO is approved. Purchases made without an
approved PO are not paid unless ratified by the CFO.
2. Approval Thresholds
Approval authority and competitive requirements depend on the total value of the purchase (excluding sales tax)
and cannot be avoided by splitting a purchase into smaller orders.

2.1 Exceptions
• Sole-source purchases need a written justification form (unique capability, compatibility or urgency)
approved one level above the normal approver.
• Emergency purchases needed to restore a production service may proceed with verbal approval of the
CTO or CFO; the PO must be raised within 2 working days.
• Recurring subscriptions are approved for the contract term and reviewed annually.
3. Vendor Onboarding and Evaluation
A vendor must be registered before its first PO. Procurement collects the vendor's NTN and sales tax
registration (STRN), active taxpayer status, bank account details on company letterhead, a signed
conflict-of-interest declaration and, for IT vendors, an InfoSec questionnaire. Vendors are re-reviewed every 2
years.
Quotations are scored using weighted criteria (Figure 2). Price alone does not decide the award, but the
lowest-priced compliant vendor must be selected unless a written justification is approved.
Figure 2. Vendor evaluation scoring weights.

4. Procure-to-Pay Process
Figure 3. Procure-to-pay workflow.
An invoice is paid only when the three-way match succeeds: the PO, the goods receipt or service acceptance,
and the vendor invoice agree on quantity, price and terms. Discrepancies are returned to the vendor within 3
working days.
4.1 Payment Terms
Table 2. Standard payment terms.
Item
Rule
Standard credit period
Net 30 days from receipt of a correct invoice
Advance payment
Up to 30% of PO value; above PKR 1,000,000 a bank guarantee is required
Payment run
Weekly on Thursday; urgent payments with CFO office approval
Withholding taxes
Income tax and sales tax withholding are deducted per Pakistan tax law and depend on the
vendor's active taxpayer status; tax certificates are issued
Invoice currency
PKR; foreign-currency contracts require Finance approval and use the State Bank rate on
the invoice date
5. Contracts, Software and Records
• Contracts above PKR 500,000 are reviewed by Legal; software, SaaS and cloud purchases are reviewed by
InfoSec before approval.
• Conflicts of interest must be declared before evaluation; an involved employee is excluded from the
decision.
• Gifts from vendors above PKR 5,000 must be reported (see Employee Handbook, NX-HR-002).
• Procurement files (requisition, quotations, evaluation, PO, GRN, invoice, payment) are retained for 7 years.
6. References
[1] Nexora Expense Policy, NX-FIN-001.
[2] Nexora Employee Handbook, NX-HR-002 (conflict of interest and gifts).
[3] Sales Tax Act, 1990 and Income Tax Ordinance, 2001 (Pakistan).
[4] Public Procurement principles: transparency, competition and value for money (adopted as internal best practice).
